requirements_summary:
Cerulean requires a reserved GPU pool across NA + EU with multi-AZ distribution. Core asks: predictable throughput for peak retail hours (Black Friday-like peaks), strict latency SLOs for interactive checkout + kiosk experiences, and failover headroom to tolerate full-AZ outage with <2x latency degradation. Specifics: target sustained throughput of 1,200 requests/min per region (avg prompt length 60 tokens, response 120 tokens), peak concurrency 800 chat sessions NA, 300 EU. Latency target p95 <= 60ms for 256-token scoped evals; p99 < 150ms. Failover headroom: 20-30% additional reserved GPUs per region as warm capacity, or cross-region spill policy with cold start constraints. Prefers A100-80GB equivalence; open to quantized LLMs if accuracy stays within 2% of baseline. KV cache replication strategy required for multi-region routing to avoid cache stampedes. Autoscale bursts up to 2x baseline for 10-30min windows; customer wants pricing clarity for bursts and reserved commit amortization. Legal requires SLA credit table and clear MTTR for region failures.

Routing policy: latency-first routing for checkout endpoints, cost/latency hybrid for recommendation batch jobs. Canary deploys required for model rollouts with automatic fallback to smaller model in event of saturation.
reserved_gpu_plan:
Customer preference: split reserved pool across 3 AZs in NA region (evenly distributed) and 2 AZs in EU region. Baseline ask: NA: 40 A100-equiv GPUs reserved (supports baseline + 25% headroom), EU: 12 A100-equiv GPUs reserved with 30% warm standby. Proposed failover strategy: NA overflow to EU during regional outage (pre-agreed RPO: 30s connection re-route, but legal concerned about data residency). Suggested warm-warm model: maintain hot prefix caches in each region with cross-region async replication; cold KV refresh allowed. Consideration: cross-region egress fees vs reserved cost - customer asked for modeled bill scenarios.

Negotiation levers requested: price tiers for 1yr vs 3yr commits, flexible burst pool credits, SLA tiers with differing credit formulas (99.95% vs 99.99%), and an option for quarterly reassessment of reserved counts based on observed token throughput.
